quotes.speaker: Jay Huff
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Huff on his past interest in creative writing
quotes.excerpt: I used to love creative writing when I was in middle school and even college some.

text_blocks.speaker: Quinn Buckner
text_blocks.text: If you want to write, what is it that you want to write about?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Huff
text_blocks.text: I don't really know yet. I used to love creative writing when I was in middle school and even college some. I remember one of my favorite stories I wrote, I forgot that I had a story due in a college creative writing class. I had no idea, had nothing done, and my professor emailed me and said, 'Hey, you forgot to turn in your story today, you can just leave it in my box.' I had nothing on me. So I spent a few hours that night writing a story about how I traveled back in time to write my essay. I included the professor's email in the story, so he knew that I had nothing done. I got a B on it. He almost gave me an A, but he gave me a B just for creativity.

quotes.speaker: Jay Huff
quotes.summary_phrase: Jay Huff on his upbringing in a basketball family
quotes.excerpt: My dad played and coached, my mom played, so it was just kind of a role model built in.

text_blocks.speaker: Quinn Buckner
text_blocks.text: How did you come to be a basketball player? Did you just grow?

text_blocks.speaker: Jay Huff
text_blocks.text: Growing up, my dad played and coached, my mom played, so it was just kind of a role model built in. I was always a little taller than everybody, but it was cool. I just kind of kept growing, and me and my friends would just spend every day playing outside on the hoop in front of the house. I would always wait for my friend to get home from school.
